title: Adaptive v3 mixed-precision compatibility shim and prefill pacing for regression mitigation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: After upstreaming FlashAttention v3 support in the runtime, we observed intermittent latency regressions and occasional OOMs on mixed-precision (fp16/amp) workloads during prefill-heavy traffic (long context seqs). This ticket implements a compatibility shim and an adaptive prefill pacing layer to safely integrate v3 kernels without widening tail latency or increasing unit cost for production customers.

Goals: (1) Provide a runtime shim that selects a guarded execution path for v3 kernels on mixed-precision models when heuristics indicate potential instability. (2) Add an adaptive prefill pacing controller that throttles/batches prefill requests dynamically to avoid simultaneous memory pressure spikes. (3) Validate with microbenchmarks, e2e load tests, and rollout canary.

Scope: Runtime and scheduler changes only. No model weight changes. Does not modify model zoo. Includes tests, perf dashboards, and a staged rollout plan.

Non-Goals: Complete v3-only optimizations (separate follow-up), hardware-specific kernel rewrites, and GPU driver changes.
acceptance_criteria: No end-to-end 99th percentile latency regression vs baseline for the canary dataset (<= 3% increase) under 2x production-ish load
No increase in OOM incidents during 48h canary run on dedicated pools
Adaptive prefill pacing reduces concurrent prefill memory spikes by >= 40% on stress tests
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rollout policy; ability to force fallback to v2 kernels via config
tasks: Design heuristic: sequence-length + kv-cache-utilization + free-memory threshold
Implement v3 compatibility shim that falls back to v2 for flagged conditions
Implement adaptive prefill pacing controller (controller + lightweight occupancy estimator)
Create microbenchmark suite for long-seq mixed-precision scenarios
Add e2e load test harness job and dashboards
Run 48h canary on dedicated cluster, collect incidents and perf traces
Author rollout doc, rollback criteria, and operator playbook
comments: 2025-02-13 -- Maya Chen: Initial spike in 99p latency observed when switching to v3 on mixed-precision LLaMA-like models; repro deck attached to spec.
2025-02-18 -- Luis Ortega: Implemented prototype shim that checks free-memory and sequence-length; simple fallthrough to v2 when threshold crossed. Prototype PR at runtime#1999.
2025-02-22 -- Kiran Patel (SRE): Verified that fallback logic prevented 2 OOMs on stress run; measured increased per-token CPU overhead ~1.8% due to checks — acceptable for now.
2025-02-27 -- Design review (PM + Eng): Agreed to make pacing controller conservative by default; create opt-in aggressive mode behind release flag.
2025-03-01 -- QA: Added mixed-precision long-seq microbenchmarks. Observed that naive prefill batching can cause short-lived memory spikes; pacing reduced spikes by ~45% in experiments.
2025-03-04 -- Luis Ortega: Preparing canary rollout doc. Next: wire metrics and start 24h canary on 2 dedicated pools next week.
risks: Shim complexity can hide regressions by masking kernel failures; pacing may add latency for tail-sensitive use-cases if misconfigured; operator burden for tuning thresholds.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag off in prod. 2) Enable in internal test cluster for 24h. 3) 24h canary on two low-risk tenants (dedicated pools). 4) 48h canary on broader dedicated fleet if metrics stable. 5) Gradual percentage rollout to hosted API with automatic rollback on SLA violations.
test_plan: Unit tests for shim logic; GPU-integration tests with CI runners; microbenchmarks for long-seq fp16 workloads; SLO-based canary verification job that fails the rollout if 99p latency or OOM counts increase beyond thresholds.
notes: Consider shipping an observability-led alert that surfaces when shim fallbacks exceed 1% of requests to detect mis-tuning. Track quantization profile interactions separately (follow-up ticket).
